items.proposed_content: Product independence turns the unweighted characteristic function into a product of local factors and the derivative-weighted transform into sums of products with marked factors. Reserving sufficiently many small unmarked factors yields arbitrarily strong polynomial Fourier decay and smooth densities; the sharper reciprocal-radius conditions r_n^{-1}=O(n) and r_n^{-1}=o(n) yield fixed and arbitrarily strong exponential decay, respectively, giving real-analytic and entire density extensions.

items.proposed_content: Finite Euler products provide an exact first stage in which ordinary almost periodicity and prime-log equidistribution identify vertical value laws with Haar laws on a finite torus; generalized Jensen and characteristic-function stability then form a second stage that transfers those laws, Jensen functions, motions, and zero-frequency statements to zeta and the chosen branch of log zeta.

items.proposed_content: Exponentiation transports the log-zeta distribution program to zeta by periodizing over every logarithmic lift and applying the change-of-variables Jacobian. The ordinary zeta density is |x|^{-2} times the lift sum of the log density, whereas derivative weighting compensates that factor; Gaussian control of the lift sums transfers smoothness and supports the later Jensen-curvature formulas while making x=0 and the multiplicity of logarithmic preimages essential features rather than removable notation.

items.proposed_content: Strict positivity of the unweighted and derivative-weighted limiting densities is proved by different resources: divergent small component lengths give phase-polygon reachability and, through tail support plus convolution, positivity of the unweighted density; the weighted density additionally requires two regular phase preimages of the same value whose derivative-like weights stay separated, preventing simultaneous degeneration after a common tail is added.

items.proposed_content: At the Re(s)=1/2 boundary, divergence of the log-Euler square-sum forces the nonzero-frequency characteristic function to collapse and the unweighted log-value density to flatten uniformly while retaining total mass. The logarithmic-potential formulas nevertheless make the Jensen functions diverge there; their slope/zero-count consequences, accumulated over the whole permitted half-plane, yield N(T)/T tending to infinity for log zeta minus any target and for zeta minus a nonzero target.

items.proposed_content: The source turns vertical value statistics into zero statistics by representing the Jensen function of f-x as the logarithmic potential of the unweighted value law, then using the area theorem to identify the curvature of that potential with the continuous density of the |f'|^2-weighted value law; integrating this curvature across real parts gives strip-zero frequency.
